sections.h2: What is Burke County, Georgia, and who owns homes there?
sections.html:
Burke County is one of Georgia's original counties, created on February 5, 1777, and it lies on the state's eastern border facing South Carolina. Waynesboro is the county seat. At 827 square miles of land it is the second-largest county in Georgia by area, and it belongs to the Augusta metropolitan area (Wikipedia).

The county's own site lists seven municipalities: Blythe, Girard, Keysville, Midville, Sardis, Vidette and Waynesboro. It calls Burke the Bird Dog Capital of the World, and hunting and fishing draw many visitors.

The Census Bureau puts the July 2025 population at 24,408, a drop of 0.8 percent from the 2020 base. For 2020 to 2024, Census QuickFacts shows a median owner-occupied value of $151,600, 70.0 percent of homes owner-occupied and 100 building permits for 2025. Sellers here are often holding farmland, timber or an older house in town, and the county's size means the parcel can be far from the courthouse.

sections.h2: Where are the Burke County tax offices?
sections.html:
Both property tax offices share a building at 524 Myrick Street in Waynesboro. The Board of Assessors is in Suite B and the tax commissioner is in Suite A. The assessor values property, and its page says the office is not responsible for tax bills and does not collect tax. The commissioner bills and collects for the county, the state and the Board of Education, and the commissioner's site says that office plays no part in setting values.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Burke County assessment?
sections.html:
You have 45 days from the notice to appeal, and the commissioner's site describes four routes. The assessor's page says assessment notices are sent to taxpayers in July, so watch the mail then.

  • Board of Equalization. The appeal goes first to the Board of Assessors, which may amend the value and send a new notice. You then have 30 days to appeal the amended notice, and an unchanged appeal is forwarded to the Board of Equalization for a hearing.
  • Hearing officer. Available only for non-homestead real property worth more than $500,000, and the hearing officer must be a state-certified appraiser.
  • Arbitration. File within 45 days, then supply a certified appraisal within 45 days of the acknowledgement. The board has 10 days to acknowledge your filing, and the hearing follows within 30 days of authorization.
  • Superior Court. A written notice goes to the Board of Assessors within 30 days of the decision.

The arbitrator's fees depend on the result. The page states that the county pays if your value is closest to the arbitrator's figure, and you pay if the board's value is closer.

sections.h2: Which Burke County homestead exemptions exist?
sections.html:
Exemptions can be filed year-round with either the commissioner or the Board of Assessors, but the application must be postmarked or received by the last day of the appeal period to count for the current year. You must own, occupy and claim the home as your residence on January 1. The commissioner's FAQ gives April 1 as the deadline for the current billing year.

The exemptions listed on the county's homestead page include:

  • S1 standard exemption, $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school, with no age or income test.
  • S3 and S4 for owners 62 and 65 with income under $10,000, with a school exemption of $10,000.
  • S5, SD, SS and SE for disabled veterans and surviving spouses of service members.
  • SG for the surviving spouse of a peace officer or firefighter killed in the line of duty.
  • L3 and L4 local school exemptions for owners 65 and older.

Refinancing does not disturb an exemption unless the deed name changes. Any vehicle you own must also be registered in Burke County. The Burke County Board of Commissioners, the Board of Education and the cities of Waynesboro, Sardis, Girard, Midville and Keysville have opted out of the statewide floating exemption.

sections.h2: What payment rules apply in Burke County?
sections.html:
The commissioner accepts cash, checks, money orders and major credit cards, and card payments add a convenience fee. You can pay online or by phone at 1-844-898-2374, and you will need your bill number.

Some answers on the commissioner's FAQ matter to anyone selling:

  • Partial payments are allowed, but interest and penalty keep accruing on the unpaid balance.
  • If the property is subject to a tax lien sale, call the commissioner before making a partial payment.
  • A property under appeal is still billed. Appeal accounts are billed at 85 percent of fair market value, and adjustments follow the final ruling.
  • A surviving spouse can petition for a year's support through an attorney or the probate court.

A non-homestead mobile home located in the county on January 1 owes tax and must display a yearly decal. Taxes not paid by the deadline carry a 10 percent penalty plus interest, and a missing decal brings a fine between $100 and $300.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Burke County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels can go to tax sale. The tax commissioner's site posted an October 6, 2026 sale date with a parcel list, so that sale has passed. The commissioner's home page links to that sale's parcel list.

Before you list, search the parcel number on the commissioner's site and confirm no earlier year is open. Burke's tax returns are also due from January 1 through April 1, and personal property that totals $7,500 or less in fair market value is exempt from ad valorem tax, except for motor vehicles, trailers and mobile homes. A buyer's attorney will check both the real property bill and any personal property or mobile home account tied to the address.

For the amount due at closing, ask the commissioner for a written payoff, and ask your closing attorney how the current year's bill is divided between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Where is the Burke County tax commissioner's office?
faqs.a: It is at 524 Myrick Street, Suite A, Waynesboro, GA 30830. The phone is 706-554-3223, and the office is open 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays and on the first and third Saturdays from 9 a.m. to noon.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Burke County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. If the Board of Assessors changes the value, you have 30 days to appeal the amended notice.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay my Burke County tax bill while an appeal is pending?
faqs.a: Yes. Appeal accounts are billed at 85 percent of fair market value, and the county adjusts the bill after the final decision.

faqs.q: Can I make a partial property tax payment in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, but interest and penalty continue on what remains unpaid. If the parcel is subject to a tax lien sale, call the commissioner before paying a partial amount.

faqs.q: What is the Burke County standard homestead exemption?
faqs.a: The S1 standard exemption takes $2,000 off assessed value for state, county and school taxes, with no age or income requirement. You must own and occupy the home on January 1 and apply by the April 1 deadline.
